correctness.rationale: Bipartite vertex-time parity strands are independent and equipotent by a one-step shift from an empty natural state. The full adoption goal saturates both, and saturation propagates naturally thereafter, giving exactly twice the strand optimum. On complete bipartite graphs next-round natural adoption depends only on opposing active cardinality, exactly captured by f and g; every weighted arc is realizable and no cheaper transfer exists. Dijkstra and a first-natural-activation lower bound prove all formulas. Full-state exhaustive cross-checks passed in 168 small biclique profiles, 3860 small bipartite instances, and 3025 uniform parameters; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Timed non-progressive influence targeting is generally hard, and the known exact class of trees does not include bicliques of both parts at least two. Heterogeneous thresholds in two wholly connected communities are natural. The theorem provides exact efficient optimization and optimal schedule reconstruction, an even-cost structural constraint for all bipartite graphs, and a genuinely multi-round two-pulse four-by-four example. This is a meaningful motivated tractability case, not a routine table value.
